claim: Mean time to compromise (MTTC) is an attacker-side effectiveness metric, with McQueen et al. as an example of the works surveyed (caption: 'MTD metrics as Cho et al. classify them, with examples from the works surveyed').
quote: The time-to-compromise ( Tpi) is defined as the time needed for an attacker to gain some level of privilege p on some system component i.
locator: preprint PDF p. 4, Sec. 3 (published pp. 49-64; printed page not in the saved copy)
issue: McQueen's metric is the expected time-to-compromise of one SCADA component, estimated analytically for risk reduction; the paper is not an MTD evaluation, and it names the quantity 'time-to-compromise' ("mean time-to-compromise" appears only for Process 1). It is the metric's origin, not an MTD example.
fix_text: Keep as the lineage root, or, if the caption's 'MTD metrics ... works surveyed' is to hold strictly, move mcqueen2006 out of the cell (cho2020, zhang2023, ho2024 carry the MTD use).

claim: Other models that time attack steps set their durations by judgement where data are missing.
quote: The estimation of time-to-compromise is particularly difficult because of the lack of reliable data. We recognize that some of the assumptions associated with our model have not been validated but we have attempted to provide justification with real data when data is available. We have used expert elicitation or have made simple assumptions when data is unavailable.
locator: preprint p. 3 (PDF p. 3), Sec. 1; worked case at preprint PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.1.2: "Somewhat arbitrarily, we de- cided to use 8 hours (one working day) as the mean time for a successful attack in Process 1"
issue: Survives the adversarial read: the source says outright that it uses expert elicitation or simple assumptions where data are unavailable, and sets a step mean 'somewhat arbitrarily'. Caveat: the 8 h was placed between two cited data points, not set from what the step does alone. Locator is the INL preprint; published pagination not saved.

claim: MTTC (as the dissertation computes it) has McQueen et al. as a source.
quote: The time-to-compromise ( Tpi) is defined as the time needed for an attacker to gain some level of privilege p on some system component i.
locator: preprint PDF p. 4, Sec. 3 (published pp. 49-64; printed page not in the saved copy)
issue: McQueen's time-to-compromise is the expected time to gain a privilege on one component, computed from a model of vulnerabilities and skill; the dissertation's MTTC is a network-goal mean over simulation runs (U0560). McQueen is the concept's origin; the operational metric is Zhang's.
fix_text: Keep (both keys together read as origin + operational use); or "\citep{mcqueen2006, zhang2023}" -> "\citep{zhang2023}, after \citep{mcqueen2006}" if the table distinguishes adaptations.

claim: MTTC is the mean time from the start of a run to the attacker reaching its goal, over the runs in which it does.
quote: Time-to-compromise is a measure of the effort expended by an attacker for a successful attack assuming effort is expended uniformly.
locator: preprint p. 3 (PDF p. 3), Sec. 1; definition at preprint PDF p. 4, Sec. 3: "The time-to-compromise ( Tpi) is defined as the time needed for an attacker to gain some level of privilege p on some system component i."
issue: McQueen supports conditioning on success ('for a successful attack') but defines TTC per component and privilege level, as a modelled expected value, not as a mean over runs from a run's start to a network goal. 'Over the runs in which it does' is a simulation estimator McQueen does not have.
fix_text: Leave the definition on zhang2023 and give McQueen the concept: "... over the runs in which it does \citep{zhang2023}, after the time-to-compromise of \citet{mcqueen2006}:" (minimal alternative: keep, if both keys are read as lineage + use).
